schema: Every claim in this repo's docs and site must point at one of these entries.
retrieval_method: fetch_page (docs.kalshi.com markdown endpoints) and PDF text extraction. Sandbox egress is limited to GitHub/PyPI/npm, so api.kalshi.com could not be called; every URL below is the official Kalshi documentation page or file that the claim was read from.

K1.title: API Environments and Endpoints
claims_supported: REST production recommended base URL is https://external-api.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2
REST production also supported: https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2
REST demo recommended base URL is https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2
REST demo also supported: https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2
WebSocket production recommended: wss://external-api-ws.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2
WebSocket production also supported: wss://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2
WebSocket demo recommended: wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2
WebSocket demo also supported: wss://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2
Credentials are not shared between demo and production
Signature covers timestamp + method + path without query string; hosts do not change the signed payload

K2.title: Test In The Demo Environment
claims_supported: Demo environment offers mock funds
Demo web UI is https://demo.kalshi.co/
Demo credentials are not shared with production
WARNING: price and behavior of markets in the demo environment may not be reflective of real markets
Demo REST root https://external-api.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2, WS wss://external-api-ws.demo.kalshi.co/trade-api/ws/v2

K3.title: API Keys
claims_supported: API keys are asymmetric key pairs; private key signs, registered public key verifies
Ed25519 (recommended, RFC 8032, 64-byte signature) and RSA 2048-bit (RSA-PSS, SHA-256, MGF1-SHA256, salt length = digest length) are supported
Headers: KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY, KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP (ms), KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE (base64)
Signature = base64(sign(timestamp + METHOD + path_without_query))
Timestamp must be within 30 seconds of Kalshi's clock or the request returns 401 header_timestamp_expired
Private key cannot be retrieved again after the key is created

K4.title: Rate Limits and Tiers
claims_supported: Token-bucket limits; most requests cost 10 tokens
Separate Read and Write buckets
429 returns error code too_many_requests; back off exponentially
GET /portfolio/balance uses its own bucket: 1/sec on Basic/Advanced, 5/sec above
Balance only changes on fills, settlements and transfers; prefer the fills WebSocket channel over polling

K5.title: Orderbook Responses
claims_supported: GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook returns orderbook_fp with yes_dollars and no_dollars arrays
Each level is [price_dollars, count_fp]; arrays are ascending, so the best bid is the last element
Order counts per level are not returned (one entry per price level, aggregated size)
Only bids are returned; YES bid at X equals NO ask at 1-X
Best YES ask = 1 - best NO bid; best NO ask = 1 - best YES bid
Unknown ticker returns 200 with empty arrays, not 404

K6.title: Kalshi Fee Schedule (PDF, effective July 7, 2026)
claims_supported: General trading (taker) fee: fees = roundup(M * 0.07 * C * P * (1-P))
Maker fee: fees = roundup(M * 0.0175 * C * P * (1-P)); maker multiplier M defaults to 0 for the general schedule
Trading fees are only charged for orders immediately matched against resting orders, unless the series has maker fees
round up means the fee plus position cost is rounded up to a centicent ($0.0001)
There is no settlement fee
Per-series taker/maker multipliers are listed in the Non-Standard Fees table; 1 means one times the general formula

K7.title: Fee Rounding
claims_supported: Trade fee is rounded up to the nearest $0.000001 (six decimals)
Direct-member balances are aligned to $0.0001; non-direct to $0.01
Net fee = trade fee + rounding fee - rebate, always >= $0

K8.title: Quick Start: WebSockets
claims_supported: WebSocket connections are authenticated during the handshake with the same three headers
WS signature pre-sign text is timestamp + GET + /trade-api/ws/v2
Subscribe with {"id":N,"cmd":"subscribe","params":{"channels":[...],"market_tickers":[...]}}
Private channels: orderbook_delta, fill, market_positions, communications, order_group_updates; public market-data channels: ticker, trade, market_lifecycle_v2, multivariate_market_lifecycle
429 too_many_requests on handshake = connection limit or opening too fast; use exponential backoff
Kalshi pings after 10s without a data message; a missing ping is not a dead connection

K9.title: Get Markets
claims_supported: GET /markets with limit (max 1000), cursor, event_ticker, series_ticker, status, min_close_ts, max_close_ts
status filter accepts unopened, open, closed, settled

Market fields include ticker, event_ticker, title, subtitle, yes_bid_dollars, yes_ask_dollars, last_price_dollars, volume_fp, volume_24h_fp, open_interest_fp, liquidity_dollars, result ('yes'/'no'/''), close_time, settlement_ts, settlement_value_dollars, rules_primary, notional_value_dollars
Fixed-point strings: *_fp counts have 2 decimals; *_dollars prices are dollar strings

K10.title: Get Market Orderbook
claims_supported: GET /markets/{ticker}/orderbook?depth=N returns orderbook_fp with aggregated sizes per price level
Response is bids only for both sides

K11.title: Get Events
claims_supported: GET /events?limit=200&status=open&with_nested_markets=true&min_close_ts=...
Event fields: event_ticker, series_ticker, title, sub_title, mutually_exclusive, strike_date, strike_period, markets[], settlement_sources[]
status filter accepts unopened, open, closed, settled
category is deprecated on events; category lives on the series

K12.title: Get Series List
claims_supported: GET /series?category=...&include_volume=true
Series fields: ticker, frequency, title, category, categories[], tags[], settlement_sources[], contract_url, contract_terms_url, fee_type, fee_multiplier
A series is a template for recurring events (e.g. daily weather in NYC)
Category filter matches any entry in categories[], case-sensitive, and the returned primary category may differ

K13.title: Create Order (V2)
claims_supported: POST /portfolio/events/orders is the V2 order create endpoint
Legacy /portfolio/orders write endpoints were removed and return 410 Gone with code deprecated_v1_order_endpoint

Required body: ticker, side (bid|ask), count (fixed-point string), price (fixed-point dollars), time_in_force (fill_or_kill|good_till_canceled|immediate_or_cancel), self_trade_prevention_type (taker_at_cross|maker)
bid = buy YES, ask = sell YES (economically buy NO)
201 response: order_id, client_order_id, fill_count, remaining_count, ts_ms; 201 means accepted, not resting
reduce_only orders are rejected unless time_in_force is immediate_or_cancel
expiration_time (unix seconds) only with good_till_canceled; GTT is not a valid API value

K14.title: Cancel Order (V2)
claims_supported: DELETE /portfolio/events/orders/{order_id}; provide market_ticker to auto-route
Returns {order_id, client_order_id, reduced_by}

K15.title: Get Balance
claims_supported: GET /portfolio/balance returns balance (cents), balance_dollars, portfolio_value (cents), updated_ts, balance_breakdown[]
The response has no explicit total-equity field; balance + portfolio_value are the two components

K16.title: Get Positions
claims_supported: GET /portfolio/positions?count_filter=position&settlement_status=all
market_positions[] fields: ticker, position_fp (signed: positive YES, negative NO), market_exposure_dollars, realized_pnl_dollars, fees_paid_dollars, total_traded_dollars, last_updated_ts
settlement_status accepts unsettled (default), settled, all

K17.title: Get Fills
claims_supported: GET /portfolio/fills returns fills[] with order_id, ticker, outcome_side (yes|no), book_side (bid|ask), count_fp, yes_price_dollars, no_price_dollars, is_taker, created_time, fee_cost, ts
outcome_side describes directional exposure: buy-yes and sell-no produce 'yes'; buy-no and sell-yes produce 'no'
Both parties trade at the same price; a fill at p with outcome_side=no is matched against an order at the same p with outcome_side=yes

K18.title: WebSocket: Market Ticker
claims_supported: ticker channel: combined and flushed once per second, one message per changed market

msg fields: market_id, market_ticker, price_dollars, yes_bid_dollars, yes_ask_dollars, volume_fp, open_interest_fp, dollar_volume, dollar_open_interest, yes_bid_size_fp, yes_ask_size_fp, last_trade_size_fp, ts (deprecated), ts_ms
Interpolation caveat: intermediate values are not sent; use trade or orderbook_delta for every change
A subscription created without a market filter cannot be changed later (error 13); unsubscribe and resubscribe to filter

K19.title: WebSocket: Public Trades
claims_supported: trade channel sends every trade immediately; market specification optional
msg fields: trade_id, market_ticker, yes_price_dollars, no_price_dollars, count_fp, taker_side, taker_outcome_side, taker_book_side, is_block_trade, ts, ts_ms

K20.title: WebSocket: Orderbook Updates
claims_supported: orderbook_delta requires market_ticker/market_tickers and sends orderbook_snapshot first, then deltas
delta msg: market_ticker, price (dollars), delta (signed contracts), side (yes|no), ts, ts_ms
When a market is determined the server sends an empty orderbook_snapshot and removes it
Conflation is opt-in via update_interval_ms 100 or 1000; default 0 is real-time
A subscription holds at most 500,000 markets

K21.title: WebSocket: Market & Event Lifecycle
claims_supported: market_lifecycle_v2 msg: market_ticker, event_type in {created, activated, deactivated, close_date_updated, determined, settled, price_level_structure_updated}
determined carries result and settlement_value; settled carries settled_ts
close_ts is present on created and close_date_updated events
This is how a market's YES/NO resolution is observed live

K22.title: Kalshi SDKs
claims_supported: Official SDKs: kalshi_python_sync, kalshi_python_async (PyPI) and kalshi-typescript (npm)
The old kalshi-python package is deprecated
REST OpenAPI spec at https://docs.kalshi.com/openapi.yaml and WebSocket AsyncAPI at https://docs.kalshi.com/asyncapi.yaml are the source of truth
Ed25519 keys need SDK 3.31.0 or later

K23.title: Get Exchange Status
claims_supported: GET /exchange/status is unauthenticated and returns exchange_active, trading_active and estimated resume times

K24.title: Kalshi starter code (official GitHub repo)
claims_supported: Official Python starter code; the README says it is example code, not an SDK
Its demo base URL constant is https://demo-api.kalshi.co (the 'also supported' demo host, not the recommended external-api host)
Its rate limiter sleeps 100 ms between calls
Source inspected at commit 6a2b0e6 (main) on 2026-11-20
K24.irregularity: Starter code targets the older demo host and does not include the V2 order path or the removed-endpoint warning, so its order examples are stale.

K25.title: Get Market Candlesticks
claims_supported: GET /series/{series_ticker}/markets/{ticker}/candlesticks?start_ts&end_ts&period_interval
period_interval valid values 1 (1 minute), 60 (1 hour), 1440 (1 day)
Candles carry yes_bid/yes_ask/trade price open/high/low/close plus volume
